title: THE FIRST FRAME
goal: Catch the first thought before it expands into a whole story.

steps.text: A trigger flickers.
Do not explain it yet.
Pin the first thought, picture, or prediction exactly as it arrived.
Put quotation marks around it.
The catch ends there; no life story, no courtroom, no spiral.

win: The trigger was captured exactly once without becoming a life story, trial, or spiral.
mindBend: A thought gains narrative power from the explanations added after it. The original thought is often much smaller.
formulaFlow: Trigger → Pause Story → Capture Thought → Quote → Close Capture

title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: Weigh visible facts on both sides before deciding what they mean.

steps.text: Imagine two trays.
Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.

win: Your verdict included supporting evidence and the facts your feeling had been overlooking.
mindBend: Emotional certainty can hide contradictory evidence simply by making one side of the file feel brighter.
formulaFlow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: Turn the feared ending into a realistic path through and beyond it.

steps.text: Picture the feared ending in one line.
Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
Move through the five steps once in your mind.
Then take the first coping action available now.

win: The worst case gained exits, support, recovery steps, and a more likely outcome before you acted.
mindBend: Catastrophe feels final when the mind shows only the ending — coping steps put time back into the picture.
formulaFlow: Name Fear → Build Exits → Add Likely → Climb Route → Act Now

title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Revise a scary probability using real reference points and opposing evidence.

steps.text: Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations.
Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
Pick a new number and remember it.
Act from the revision, not the original alarm.

win: Your second estimate differed from the alarm number because actual evidence had entered the calculation.
mindBend: Fear often reports probability as intensity. A strong feeling can sound like a statistic without being one.
formulaFlow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence

title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Own your real share of a problem without carrying everyone else's.

steps.text: Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
Make sure all slices together equal 100.
Focus only on your true share.
Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

win: Responsibility shrank to your actual slice, and one repair matched only what belonged to you.
mindBend: Personalising turns influence into total causation; sharing the pie restores causes that guilt had erased.
formulaFlow: Imagine Pie → Share Slices → Check Whole → Find Slice → Choose Repair

title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: Keep several explanations alive until new evidence separates them.

steps.text: Keep the event fixed.
Invent three models for why it happened.
Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

win: One event produced multiple testable possibilities instead of a single prediction dressed as certainty.
mindBend: Fortune telling feels convincing because the mind selects one future before reality has had a chance to vote.
formulaFlow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals

title: THE RULE UNDER THE RULE
goal: Find the hidden rule beneath a painful thought without automatically obeying it.

steps.text: Picture the painful thought.
Ask, ‘If that were true, what would it mean about me, others, or life?’ Answer quickly, then ask once more.
Continue only until one stable rule repeats.

win: A repeating rule became visible and stayed boxed as something to inspect rather than follow.
mindBend: Many surface thoughts are messengers for an older rule. Finding the rule reveals what has actually been steering.
formulaFlow: Picture Painful → Ask Meaning → Continue Stable → Box Rule → Apply Today

title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET

goal: Track how confident predictions compare with what actually happens over time.

steps.text: Before an uncertain event, remember four items: prediction, confidence %, deadline, and what counts as a hit.

mindBend: Memory quietly edits old predictions after the outcome. Recording the forecast first exposes calibration instead of hindsight.
formulaFlow: Count Hit → Keep Result → Calculate → Spot Bias

title: ONE NOTCH, NOT THE STORY
goal: Lower the current alarm one notch without touching the memory itself.

steps.text: Rate the current alarm from 0 to 10 without explaining why.
Pick one present-day cue: your feet, cool water, a stable surface, or a familiar voice.
Use that cue for twenty seconds while keeping your eyes open.
Rate the alarm once more and stop; no memory review is required.

win: The alarm had a before-and-after number without needing any contact with the memory.
mindBend: Relief can come from changing the present body state; the past does not have to be opened to create a shift.
formulaFlow: Rate Alarm → Pick Cue → Use Cue → Rate Again

safety.raw:
PAUSE
Use only present-day sensory cues. Do not deliberately bring up traumatic images, sensations, or details. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less oriented, and connect with qualified human support.
This is present-day grounding only, not trauma treatment.
safety.pause: Use only present-day sensory cues. Do not deliberately bring up traumatic images, sensations, or details. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less oriented, and connect with qualified human support.

options: CLEAR SHIFT — the intensity dropped or feels more workable
PARTLY — one step helped
NO SHIFT — the alarm or urge is still strong
LESS STEADY — stop and use support

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Strengthen one real body signal of steadiness instead of searching only for what feels wrong.

steps.text: Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
Add only that support.

win: A specific steady sensation was located, described, and supported by one thing that increased it slightly.
mindBend: Stability can be quiet enough to miss. Attention often amplifies alarm simply because alarm is easier to notice.
formulaFlow: Locate Bodily → Describe Boundaries → Ask Memory → Add Support

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Let the body give a whole-picture response before analysis takes over.

steps.text: Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
Leave the answer unpolished.

win: An image, phrase, posture, or felt texture arrived and was checked for a small inner fit.
mindBend: The body can summarise a situation before language has organised it; the first useful signal may be global rather than verbal.
formulaFlow: Bring Mind → Ask Body → Check Whether → Leave Raw

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: Let a safe defensive impulse finish in miniature instead of freezing halfway.

steps.text: Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
Observe whether the body receives an ending.

win: A tiny push, turn, step, shield, or no reached a natural endpoint and returned to neutral.
mindBend: An unfinished defence can keep feeling current. A small completed movement may give the body the ending the original impulse never reached.
formulaFlow: Small → Let Unfold → Stop Completion → Observe Whether

steps.text: After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release.

title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
goal: Anchor to today's date using the room, an exit, and reachable support.

steps.text: Say today's full date and your current location aloud.
Read the names of three ordinary objects directly in front of you.
Point to the nearest safe exit without moving toward the past memory.
Name one person or service available in the present.
Keep eyes open and return attention to the whole room.

win: Today's date, current location, ordinary objects, a safe exit, and a present-day helper all became explicit.
mindBend: Trauma memory can erase timestamps. Ordinary present facts act like metadata the alarm response did not carry with it.
formulaFlow: Name Date → Read Objects → Locate Exit → Name Support → Return Room

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: Fit the conversation to the amount you can safely handle right now.

steps.text: Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

win: You stopped at the chosen sentence limit and made the condition for reopening clear.
mindBend: A conversation can be honest without being unlimited; bandwidth is a boundary, not a measure of care.
formulaFlow: Read Bandwidth → Choose Size → Send Signal → Set Reopen

goal: Lower the panic load without testing your heart sensations or forcing your breathing.

steps.text: Keep your eyes open and name three edges or corners you can see.

win: Your attention widened to the room, one movement slowed, and a safe person was brought into the moment.
mindBend: Body alarm becomes louder when every sensation is treated as evidence needing inspection. External orientation interrupts that closed feedback loop.
formulaFlow: See Room → Slow Move → Call Support
